extracted.intended_audience: War Department officials, military administrators, and military lawyers handling discharges
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, standards, and procedural guidance governing when and how enlisted men and officers may be discharged (including effective dates, notices, character notations, boards, insanity/minority issues, and special-case statutes). Intended to guide administrative and legal decisions about discharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of election to be discharged at close of war
rubrics_metrics.description: A soldier's waiver to elect at the close of the war to be discharged is of no effect; an application after the war must be made within a reasonable time of the close of the war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Held that the war closed April 11, 1899, and an application of June 13, 1899, was not within a reasonable time unless the soldier could not have acted sooner by reasonable diligence. Whether he was so situated is to be determined by those in charge of discharging soldiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discharge entitlement at close of war when under charges or sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: Men enlisted or reenlisted in the Regular Army during the Spanish War will be granted discharges at the close of the war upon individual applications, but will not be discharged if under charges, awaiting trial, or serving sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General Orders 40, Adjutant General's Office, 1898, was not intended to relieve them from consequences of military offenses (C. 5787, Feb. 3, 1899).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discharge for transfer to another government department requires showing public interest benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: Discharge requested because the soldier's services were desired in another department rests upon grounds of expediency and whether the public interest will be benefited by the discharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request should affirmatively state what benefit to the Government will result; mere hope of securing employment in another branch without a showing of desire by that branch is insufficient (C. 15717, Jan. 6, 1911).

rubrics_metrics.name: Liberal construction of 'for the convenience of the Government'
rubrics_metrics.description: Act of May 11, 1908 should be given a liberal construction to carry out Congress's purpose to encourage reenlistments; discharges 'for the convenience of the Government' are to be liberally construed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All soldiers honorably discharged by the Government on its own motion or for its own advantage after serving over half their enlistment and before expiration are equally deserving; discharges for services no longer needed, to be immediately reenlisted, or for disability are 'for the convenience of the Government' (U. 23547; 28327).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'character' notation on discharge
rubrics_metrics.description: The notation as to character entered upon a soldier's discharge refers to his character regarded both as a soldier and as a man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct answer to inquiry (C. 15359, Oct. 10, 1903).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointing board under Army Regulations directory only
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions relating to appointment of a board of officers to determine facts relative to a soldier's character are directory only and do not affect validity of an executed discharge if the regulations were not observed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited decisions: C. 5943, March, 1899; 12942, July 11, 1902.

rubrics_metrics.name: 30-day notice and board requirement applies only at expiration of enlistment term
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations that require a company commander to notify a soldier at least 30 days prior to discharge and convene a board to determine honesty/faithfulness apply only to discharges at expiration of term of enlistment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Has never been regarded as restricting the Secretary of War's authority under the fourth article of war to annul an enlistment whenever public interest dictates (C. 20754; 23259).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discharge without honor for confined soldier requires prior board action
rubrics_metrics.description: A discharge without honor should not be given to a soldier confined in the guardhouse at date of expiration of term awaiting trial or result of trial or serving a sentence which does not involve dishonorable discharge, without the previous action of a board of officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to paragraph 156 A.R., 1910 for date of discharge in such cases (C. 28556, June 19, 1911).

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for consensus before discharge without honor for 'not honest and faithful' service
rubrics_metrics.description: A soldier cannot be discharged without honor on account of service 'not honest and faithful' without the consensus of opinion of the company commander, the board, and the convening authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a second board was convened improperly after a board found honest service and convening authority disapproved, there was no authority for the second board and the soldier was entitled to an honorable discharge (C. 19364, Mar. 19, 1906).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on altering company commander's character entry; Secretary of War's corrective power
rubrics_metrics.description: A War Department will not be legally justified in directing a company commander to issue another certificate changing his entry that service was 'not honest and faithful.' However the Secretary of War may, if in his opinion facts justify, enter on the man's discharge his own opinion that the service was 'honest and faithful.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains interplay between local commander's certification and Secretary's authority to amend or annotate discharge (C. 12942, July 11, 1902).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraudulent enlistment findings with prior dishonorable discharge statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A soldier who applied for enlistment and stated he had been dishonorably discharged previously, but was enlisted, is not necessarily guilty of fraudulent enlistment and appears entitled to discharge with service 'honest and faithful.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example case (C. 6599, June 17, 1899).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper characterization of discharge must reflect honest and faithful service
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a soldier's service has been honest and faithful, discharge without honor was improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case citation (C. 2230, Apr., 1896).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of conduct constituting 'not honest and faithful' service
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain specific acts have been held to render service 'not honest and faithful' — e.g., absenting himself to avoid overseas service, continuing association with a known prostitute after being directed to discontinue, marrying a well-known prostitute, arrest/conviction by civil authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations include C. 12307; C. 17583; C. 29114; C. 23259. These function as substantive examples for character determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Erasure of 'No objection to reenlistment is known to exist' implies objection exists and must be explained
rubrics_metrics.description: When the preparer of a discharge erases the remark 'No objection to his reenlistment is known to exist,' the erasure constitutes an official statement that some objection to reenlistment exists and the company commander should note the reasons under 'Remarks' on the back of the certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objections may be varied (carelessness, inability in arms/drill, fear of horses, physical affection not impairing efficiency, defects of temper). Purpose is to enable official inquiry (C. 24004, Mar. 10, 1909).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minority cannot by himself avoid enlistment; parent/guardian application required
rubrics_metrics.description: A soldier cannot himself avoid his contract of enlistment on the ground of minority and abandon service at pleasure; release on this ground can be obtained only on application of parent or guardian entitled to his services and must be made before he attains majority and ratifies his contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple precedents cited (P. 58, 142, Feb., 1893; others).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence standards to prove minority
rubrics_metrics.description: The War Department generally requires the age of an alleged minor to be shown by affidavits of both parents if living, or affidavit of surviving parent/guardian supported by affidavits of at least two other respectable persons cognizant of the fact, or by an officially authenticated church or court record; if practicable, accompanied by a judge's certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice guidance (R. 53, 53, Oct., 1886).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign birth proof requirements for minority claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicant born abroad (e.g., Bermuda), evidence of age should include a transcript of the official parish or public register of births signed by the proper custodian and certified by the United States consul; baptismal transcript insufficient if birth register exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case guidance (P. 43, 77, Sept., 1890).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marriage or parent's foreign domicile can defeat minority discharge claim
rubrics_metrics.description: An application by a parent for discharge of a minor soldier may be denied where the soldier had married (which in some jurisdictions is an emancipation) or where the parent/guardian is domiciled abroad (e.g., in France), viewed as having emancipated the child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations: P. 53, 105, Apr., 1892; P. 62, 132, Oct., 1893. Marriage/emancipation law of local jurisdiction controls effect on parental rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental practice warns parents of consequences when pressing minority claim
rubrics_metrics.description: When parents apply for discharge on minority grounds they are informed the soldier is punishable for enlisting without their consent, and that if they press the matter charges will be prepared and the soldier charged; if convicted, penalties may include dishonorable discharge, forfeiture of pay, confinement, and later release to parents if sentence doesn't include dishonorable discharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific administrative practice cited with case references (C. 16379; 17964).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public interest and criminal process may override parental right to discharge
rubrics_metrics.description: Fraudulent enlistment of a minor is punishable; if steps should be taken to punish the soldier the interests of the public in administration of justice are paramount to parental rights and the soldier must abide consequences before the right to discharge is passed upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple authorities cited (U. 50, 680, Aug., 1886; others).

rubrics_metrics.name: Soldier's right to be discharged at expiration of enlistment and duty of superior
rubrics_metrics.description: A soldier is entitled to his discharge as of the date of the expiration of the stipulated period of service for which he enlisted; he cannot discharge himself but a proper military superior is charged with the duty of discharging him on that date and neglect or refusal is at the superior's peril.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desertion does not constitute discharge
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of desertion does not operate as a discharge: the name of a deserter is dropped from the rolls and is not again taken up until apprehension or surrender, but he is in no sense discharged from the Army.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precedents P. 63, 30, Dec, 1890.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discharge dating when soldier held beyond term for lost time or convenience
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a soldier is held in service after term expiration to make up lost time under article 48 or by court-martial sentence, the discharge should be dated as of the date of actual separation and that fact should be noted on the discharge; similar rule applies when held beyond expiration for convenience of the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 18438, June 26, 1908. Ensures pay and record reflect actual separation date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot legally muster out or discharge a serving person as of prior date
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer or soldier actually serving to a given date cannot legally be mustered out or discharged as of a prior date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple citations (R. 29, 598, Jan., 1870; others).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of discharge tied to actual or constructive notice
rubrics_metrics.description: A discharge takes effect from the date upon which notice of such discharge is served upon the person to be discharged; service may be actual or constructive. Constructive notice by lodging at the place where the person should be is accepted, and absence for his own convenience doesn't allow him to claim lack of notice. But lodging notice with prison/post commander for a confined person might be insufficient; safest to give actual notice if present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case law: B. 29, 598; C. 15403; C. 1289; C. 16010; C. 5632; C. 11712; C. 27724. Distinguish actual discharge vs certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discharge certificate is evidence but not the discharge; various modes of notice suffice
rubrics_metrics.description: The discharge certificate (often called the discharge) is not the discharge itself; actual or constructive delivery is proper notice but informing the soldier verbally or otherwise constitutes equally effective notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 1570; 1916; 5632; 9556; 16938; 17700. Certificate is evidentiary, not the operative act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling discharge when soldier incapacitated or in hospital
rubrics_metrics.description: If a soldier was notified of discharge while sick in a hospital, the discharge date is the date notice was served; conversely, if too sick at enlistment expiration to receive notice, he is not discharged at expiration but held until notice can be served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: C. 11712 (May 10/Sept 15, 1901) and C. 26240 (Feb. 10, 1910). When in confinement, certificate may be held in escrow until release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discharge rules for insane soldiers and authority required
rubrics_metrics.description: An insane soldier cannot be discharged except by order of the Secretary of War under authority permitting discharge of patients in the Government Hospital for the Insane; if lucid intervals exist, notice during such interval is sufficient; if insanity existed before enlistment, discharge should be without honor and turned over to civilian authorities; government not obliged to send such patients to the Government Hospital; if insanity not incurred in line of duty, return to place of enlistment and discharge without transfer is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations: P. 61, 79; C. 11712; 15403; 19208; 20066. Additional practice and policy notes included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of notice for soldiers at Government Hospital for the Insane
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an enlistment expired while a soldier was undergoing treatment at the Government Hospital for the Insane and a discharge on surgeon's certificate of disability issued, such discharge is complete irrespective of degree of insanity or of notice being given through a committee or guardian; service of notice should be made through the superintendent of the hospital.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy for insane Philippine Scouts
rubrics_metrics.description: Soldiers of the Philippine Scouts are entitled, when insane, to be admitted into the Government Hospital for the Insane; due to cost and undesirability of transporting to Washington, advisable to contract for care, maintenance, and treatment at any asylum in the Philippine Islands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 15996, Jan. 16, 1907. Administrative policy recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date for discharge where sentence commuted or death sentence commuted
rubrics_metrics.description: When a soldier's sentence to death was commuted to imprisonment for life, his discharge took effect on the date upon which actual or constructive notice of the sentence as commuted was served on him; the discharge involved was a dishonorable discharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discharge entitlement for soldiers awaiting civil trial at term expiration
rubrics_metrics.description: A soldier held in custody awaiting trial by civil authorities at date of expiration of service is entitled to be discharged by reason of expiration the same as if not under arrest; unless his service otherwise warrants, he is entitled to an honorable discharge irrespective of subsequent civil conviction or acquittal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escrow of discharge certificate does not effect discharge while subject to military jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: When a discharge without honor was deposited with a prison officer in escrow to be delivered upon termination of military proceedings, the soldier was not discharged on the date the discharge was furnished the prison officer; he remained in service subject to court-martial jurisdiction and pleas in bar that he was a civilian should be overruled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U. 13016; 15133; 17380. Distinguishes physical custody of certificate from operative discharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dishonorable discharge execution requires promulgating order receipt at execution place
rubrics_metrics.description: A dishonorable discharge cannot be executed until the order promulgating such sentence has been received at the place where it is to be executed; if to take effect forthwith it should be dated when the order is received; the soldier is entitled to pay to include the date of discharge; if confinement also awarded, certificate is committed to custody to be held until confinement executed. Official publication alone does not effect discharge without notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P. 41, 86; C. 1767; C. 404; C. 3063; C. 16010. Addresses timing and pay consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for certificates not delivered due to escape or other reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: When a dishonorable discharge certificate was executed but not delivered due to the escape of the party discharged, the soldier was nevertheless separated from the service by the dishonorable discharge at that date and the certificate should be placed on file in the War Department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to fix future effective discharge dates and the role of notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The President or Secretary of War has the right to fix a day in future when discharge shall become operative, and the date should be chosen with regard to the time when notice of the discharge can be served; when an officer serving at an isolated station is ordered discharged on a date the order is issued in Washington the order becomes effective when the officer receives notice of his discharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 16823, Sept. 13, 1904. Emphasizes notice dependency for remote/isolated personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discharge by reason of successor's appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Senate declined to confirm a nomination and the President appointed another man to the position, the first officer was discharged on the date when the President signed the commission of the second officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 17480, Feb. 2, 1905. Administrative effect of appointments on incumbents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discharge effect when volunteer regiment mustered out but court-martial sentence void
rubrics_metrics.description: A Volunteer soldier sentenced by a mixed court to dishonorable discharge and imprisonment, where sentence later held null and void because Regular officers sat, was discharged from the service on the date when his regiment was mustered out and the discharge was without honor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 12103; 1571; 14643. Addresses interplay of court composition and mustering out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dropping from rolls by commanding general constitutes discharge when notice received
rubrics_metrics.description: An order by a commanding general directing certain men be dropped from the rolls is an order of the commanding officer of a department discharging them from the service within the meaning of the fourth article of war; their contracts were terminated the day they received notice of such order, though they may not have been furnished the usual discharge certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting a man at liberty and saying 'dropped from rolls' may amount to discharge
rubrics_metrics.description: If a man was set at liberty and told he 'has been dropped from his company rolls' and 'if he believes he has any just claim he can present it,' that act constituted discharge and a later court-martial should have accepted a plea in bar that he had been discharged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 16938; related citations. Practical lesson on verbal orders and administrative effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer mustering-out rule does not include deserters at large
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule published in general orders that when Volunteer troops are mustered out the entire regiment is considered mustered out at same time and place, did not include deserters at large who had been dropped from the rolls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 10141, Apr. 3, 1901. Clarifies limits of mass mustering rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discharge certificate as legal evidence but not conclusive; correction of errors
rubrics_metrics.description: A formal certificate of discharge signed as required is legal evidence of the fact of discharge and circumstances stated; it is furnished primarily for the soldier's use but is not conclusive upon the Government when contradicted by record or better evidence. If entries (like date of enlistment) are erroneous, the War Department may correct by substituting a new certificate or by indorsing a corrective statement on the old certificate; discharge is complete without final statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations: P. 51, 126; P. 149, 87; C. 11883; 11741; 11820. Practical remedies for defective certificates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature authority on discharge certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: A commanding officer who is not in the same regiment as the soldier will sign the discharge certificate of a soldier under his command only when no field officer of the enlisted man's regiment is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 13594, Nov. 6, 1902. Governs proper signatory placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory entitlement to discharge certificates for specified groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Under acts providing relief (e.g., Feb. 24, 1897 or Apr. 14, 1890) certain officers and enlisted men of Volunteer forces or those who served under assumed names are entitled to have discharge certificates furnished them; certificates may be later completed by signature if defective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 3021; P. 60, 354; C. 10889. Shows interaction of statutory relief and certificate issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: War Department may issue new certificate when value impaired by erroneous later entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an honorable discharge certificate has had its value impaired by a later erroneous entry thereon, there is no legal objection to the War Department issuing a new certificate containing no reference to the erroneous entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P. 34, 222; C. 1793; C. 11883. Administrative remedial ability to restore certificate utility.
